 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Jitendra Kumar Shrivastava, Advoc
 Ms. Sama Sinha, Advocate
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Kumar Veerendra Narayan, App
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice S. B. Pd. Singh
 Oral Order
In compliance of the order dated 07.04.2025, both the parties along with their respective counsel are present in Chamber.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for the State.
3.

The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Mahila P.S. Case No. 08 of 2023 for the offence under Sections 341, 342, 323, 504, 506, 379, 498A and 34 of the I.P.C.
4.
It is a case of matrimonial dispute between the parties in which the informant has alleged that her marriage was solemnised with the petitioner on 12.06.2011 and out of her Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.31150 of 2024(10) dt.07-04-2025 wedlock, three children were born.
It is further alleged that after her marriage, she was usually abused and beaten up by her husband after being instigated by his mother.
It is also alleged that her husband has solemnised second marriage with another girl.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is quite innocent and has falsely been implicated in this present case.

The petitioner has not solemnised second marriage, whereas,
the informant has eloped with a boy who is said to have solemnised marriage with him.

From the bare perusal of F.I.R., it will appear that neither the time of occurrence nor the date of application is mentioned in the F.I.R. and it speaks in volume about the false implication of the petitioner in the Lalan Paswan @ Lalan Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156153843/
1 instant case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The informant herself left her matrimonial house on her own volition with her parents to go to her 'maika' from there she eloped with a boy of her own choice about 18 months ago.
6. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant opposes the prayer for bail.

7. During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is ready to keep his wife with full honour and dignity despite of this fact that informant is Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.31150 of 2024(10) dt.07-04-2025 living adulterous life with another boy but informant is not ready to go with the petitioner without any valid and just cause.
Keeping in view the aforesaid facts, this Court is inclined to extend him the privilege of anticipatory bail.

8. Let the petitioner be released on bail in the event of arrest or surrender within a period of four weeks from the fate of receipt of this order, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten thousand)
each with two sureties of like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Muzaffarpur, in connection with Mahila P.S. Case No. 08 of 2023 subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
(S. B. Pd. Singh, J) Ankit Kumar/-
U T Lalan Paswan @ Lalan Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156153843/
